headline: Spain's Press Suffocates Austria from Start to Finish
story: Spain controlled this from the opening whistle, establishing a smothering possession game (59%) that left Austria chasing shadows. The early stages saw the Austrians pressed into submission, unable to build from the back as Spain's forwards harried them into endless turnovers. The breakthrough came at 36 minutes—almost inevitable—and from that point the match was merely a procession. Spain's fullbacks Porro and Cucurella operated like additional midfielders, stretching the Austrians further.

The numbers tell a brutal story. Spain's ball recovery averaged 12.1 seconds against Austria's laboured 20.8, a gap that reflects the gulf in midfield control. Oyarzabal (8.8) thrived in the chaos, as Spain's press phases multiplied (9.4 to 5.7). Austria never troubled the Spanish goal—zero shots on target, an xG of just 0.25—while Spain manufactured 23 attempts from an xG of 2.25, converting three by the 89th minute. The second goal at 66 minutes essentially closed proceedings.

keyMoment.text: Spain's second goal rendered Austria's task impossible; the class gulf was now absolute.

home.verdict: Press dominance and ruthless conversion overcame an overwhelmed opponent.
points: Ball recovery 12.1s versus Austria's 20.8s created an eight-second gulf; the differential won the midfield war.
Nine high-press phases forced 51 turnovers; relentless pressing denied Austria any build-up platform.
23 shots (2.25 xG) converted three times; shot volume and clinical finishing secured a routine victory.

away.verdict: Helpless against Spain's press; no answer in midfield or attack.
points: Ball recovery 20.8s (Spain's 12.1s) meant Austria couldn't escape the press; build-up football was impossible.
Zero shots on target and xG 0.25 shows complete attacking void; Schmid and Sabitzer were isolated and ineffective.
Only 5.7 high-press phases versus Spain's 9.4 meant Austria defended for 90 minutes; control never materialised.

statLine: Spain recovered possession every 12.1 seconds; Austria required 20.8—a nine-second chasm that left their midfield suffocated and leaderless.
